exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: According to the booklet, what are Australian values based on?
options: Wealth, tradition and loyalty to one’s family
Freedom, respect, fairness and equality of opportunity
explanation: These values are described as central to Australia remaining a secure, prosperous and peaceful place to live. Citizenship is about living them out every day.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Australian values based on freedom, respect, fairness and equality of opportunity

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: You should follow the law even if no one is watching.
explanation: Commitment to the Rule of Law is an Australian value. Everybody should obey the law at all times, or face penalties.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: You should follow the law even if no one is watching.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Australian laws apply only to Australian citizens.
explanation: The law applies to everyone who is in Australia. Whatever your background or culture, you must follow Australian laws.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Australian laws apply to all people in Australia.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Who determines Australia’s laws?
explanation: Australia is a parliamentary democracy. Because citizens vote for the people who sit in parliament, they are involved in how the country is governed.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Our laws are determined by parliaments elected by the people.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Under the Rule of Law, who is above the law?
explanation: All Australians are equal in relation to the law. Laws and legal systems protect everyone and apply to everyone.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: no person or group is above the law

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Voting is compulsory in Australia.
explanation: Compulsory voting shows how important taking part in elections is. The power of the government comes from the people who vote.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Voting is compulsory in Australia.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: A group of people protest peacefully against a decision of the government. Is that allowed in Australia?
options: Only if they are all citizens
Only with a minister’s written permission
No: protesting against the government is illegal
Yes: tolerance of peaceful public protest is an essential part of democracy
explanation: Freedom of speech lets people say what they think and protest peacefully. Protests must stay within the law.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: tolerance of peaceful public protest is an essential part of democracy

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Freedom of speech means it is acceptable to promote violence against a group of people because of their religion.
explanation: People may express their ideas freely so long as it is within the law. Promoting violence against a person or group is against Australian values and the law.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: It is never acceptable to promote violence against another person or group of people

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Newspapers, television and radio outlets have the same freedom of speech as individuals.
explanation: People are free to say and write what they think about any topic. The booklet says the news media have the same freedom.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Newspapers, television and radio outlets have the same freedom.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Can a person in Australia be compelled to join an organisation?
options: No: nobody can be compelled to join an organisation or forced to leave it
explanation: Freedom of association means people join or leave groups voluntarily. That covers political parties, trade unions and religious, cultural or social groups.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Individuals cannot be compelled to join an organisation or forced to leave it.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Religious laws have legal status in Australia.
explanation: People are free to follow any religion, but religious practices must not break Australian laws. Australian law must be followed by everyone, even where it differs from religious laws.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Religious laws have no legal status in Australia.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Which of these are against the law in Australia even when they are religious or cultural practices?
explanation: Some religious or cultural practices break Australian law. Polygamy and forced marriage can lead to severe penalties, including imprisonment.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: forced marriage, are against the law in Australia

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Under Australian law, two men or two women can marry each other.
explanation: Australian society values the equal rights of all people, regardless of gender or sexual orientation. Two people can marry each other under the law.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: including marriage between two men or two women

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: A woman and a man apply for the same job. The woman has better qualifications and skills. What does the booklet say?
options: It is her right to get the job ahead of the man
The older applicant should be chosen
The man should be chosen first
explanation: Men and women have equal rights and equal access to employment. It is against the law to discriminate against a person because of their gender.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: it is a right for a woman to get a job ahead of a man, if she has better qualifications and skills

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: A wife wants a divorce but her husband wants the marriage to continue. Can she apply for one?
options: Only after ten years of marriage
Yes: either spouse may apply to the courts
No: only the husband may apply
explanation: Divorce is acceptable in Australia. Either a husband or a wife may apply, even if the other wishes to continue the marriage.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Either a husband or a wife may apply for a divorce to the courts

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Physical violence against a spouse or partner is a criminal offence in Australia.
explanation: Men and women are protected by the law from intimidation and violence. Violence against a spouse or partner is never acceptable.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: it is a criminal offence in Australia

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: According to the idea of a “fair go”, on what should getting a job be based?
explanation: Everyone deserves an equal opportunity to succeed. When an organisation fills a job, the law supports choosing the person with the best skills and experience.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: a person should get a job based on their skills and experience

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: What is the age of sexual consent in Australia?
options: 16 or 17, depending on the state or territory
explanation: Australia has very strict laws about the age of consent. It is 16 or 17 depending on the state or territory where you live.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: which is 16 or 17 depending on which state or territory you reside in

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: A police officer makes a lawful request of you. What should you do?
options: Obey only if you are a citizen
Ignore it unless it is in writing
explanation: The lawful actions of the police should be supported. All Australians commit to following the law.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: You should obey a lawful request from the police

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Verbal abuse is legal in Australia as long as there is no physical violence.
explanation: Individuals must respect the freedom and dignity of others. Violence of any kind, including verbal and physical abuse, is illegal.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Violence of any kind, including verbal and physical abuse, is illegal.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: What do mutual respect and tolerance mean, according to the booklet?
options: Avoiding people who disagree with you
Listening to others and respecting their views, even when they differ from your own
explanation: Australians believe in peaceful disagreement. People should be tolerant of each other where they find that they disagree.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: even when they are different from your own

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Someone shares racially offensive material on the internet. What does the booklet say about this?
options: Racism has no place in Australia, and this is an example of it
It only matters at a sporting event
It is acceptable in a private group
It is acceptable if it is meant as a joke
explanation: Racism includes creating or sharing racially offensive material online or in other publications. It also includes racially abusive comments in a public place or at a sporting event.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Racism has no place in Australia.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: What is “mateship”?
options: Helping each other in times of need
explanation: Mateship might mean taking a meal to an elderly neighbour or driving a friend to a medical appointment. It is behind Australia’s strong tradition of community service and volunteering.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: We help each other in times of need.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Why does the booklet say it is important to learn to speak English?
options: It helps to get an education and a job, and to integrate into the community
It is the only language allowed in public
It lowers the tax you pay
It is needed to get a driver’s licence
explanation: English is valued as the national language and as something that unifies society. People living in Australia should make an effort to learn it.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: it helps to get an education, a job, and better integrate into the community

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: You suspect a neighbour may be planning a serious crime. What should you do?
options: Report it to Australian government authorities as soon as possible
explanation: Everyone has a responsibility to help protect Australian society. Reporting such concerns helps to protect the safety of the community.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: they should report this to Australian government authorities as soon as possible

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: What is dual citizenship?
options: Holding the citizenship of Australia and of another country at the same time
Being a citizen of two Australian states
explanation: Australian citizens may also hold the citizenship of another country if that country’s laws allow. They must still follow all Australian laws while in Australia.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: This is known as dual, or multiple, citizenship.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: An Australian citizen who is also a citizen of another country must still follow all Australian laws while in Australia.
explanation: Dual citizenship does not change this. Some Australian laws must be followed by Australian citizens even when they are overseas.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: an Australian citizen within Australia must follow all Australian laws at all times

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Someone uses social media to share official government secrets. How does the booklet describe this?
options: As acceptable if the secrets are true
As a matter only for public servants
explanation: Australian society is based on shared obligations not to undermine Australia’s interests and security. Sharing official secrets is given as an example of doing so.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: using social media to share official government secrets would be undermining Australia’s interests

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: What must applicants for Australian citizenship undertake to do about English, if it is not their native language?
options: Pass a university course in English
Make reasonable efforts to learn it
explanation: English is valued as the national language. Applicants whose first language is not English must undertake to make reasonable efforts to learn it.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: must undertake to make reasonable efforts to learn the English language

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Which of these is an example of cyber abuse given in the booklet?
options: Sending an email to a friend
explanation: Online abuse is not accepted in Australia. Examples include stalking a person online and sharing sexual photos or videos without consent, and many forms are illegal.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: stalking a person online
